The Requirement in Italics

斜体字写出的入学要求 · 647 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A college held an orientation seminar for applicants. Neri wanted a vocational diploma in accountancy and a scholarship. The dean welcomed undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral candidates in the gymnasium. A former student described her entrepreneurial career. A scholar from an academy spoke about excellence in mathematics. Another described a preparatory course. Neri had a night school certificate. When a faculty member mentioned a graduate degree, she put down her form. A counselor asked which requirement she thought denied her admittance.

2Neri showed him the handbook. A line in italics said that a placement interview was compulsory for "the graduate course." In the next paragraph an unmarked line described a different requirement for a vocational course. Neri had mistaken the possessive pronoun in that paragraph for a reference to the graduate course. The wording was grammatical. Its layout hid the connection. The counselor asked her to bring a transcript and show him what she thought each sentence meant.

3A language educator examined the passage with Neri. She used plain notation to put each noun above its pronoun. A demonstrative pointed to the graduate course. A singular noun belonged to the line below, while a plural pronoun referred to the students. An adverb had changed the emphasis in a long declarative sentence. A short imperative could instruct the reader more clearly. They discussed the grammatical role of an infinitive and moved a comma. Neri could comprehend the instruction once its key parts had visible links.

4The questionnaire asked for a surname in alphabetical order and the applicant's discipline. Neri copied "economics" from an example rather than accountancy from the list. A secretarial intern sent it to the wrong professor. The mistake was easy to fix. The counselor asked whether it showed a broader issue with the examples. He invited a diligent student to compare them with their online counterparts. Several used vocabulary a first-time applicant would not recognize.

5They checked another page listing the programs. A bachelor in psychology had different tuition from an associate degree in education. A doctorate in sociology could carry a fellowship. An introductory class in geography or journalism used another deadline. Neri had assumed each example applied to her. A comparative chart showed which qualification mattered. A student of zoology checked whether the same chart worked for her. It also gave her an idea of which specialization she could choose after admission.

6At the interview a researcher asked what experience Neri had. She described an internship where a conscientious handyman taught her to compare payments with bills. She found a repeated charge. An expert in accounting asked her to give a verbal explanation of the correction. Her answer showed analytic skill and more relevance than a general claim about career advancement. They discussed whether she wanted to specialize in business, work with an entrepreneur, or continue with an academic degree.

7The revised handbook began each route with a descriptive paragraph. A sociologist checked whether the example assumed all applicants came from a privileged family. A journalist from the student paper spotted the scholarship deadline under the wrong heading. The dean appointed a trustee to provide oversight and asked both to collaborate. They removed an ironic phrase that had sounded like an exclamation. At commencement, the college gave the old form to its library as an illustrative example.

8Neri helped test the signs after her offer arrived. An interpreter checked one version, and a student with editorial expertise checked another. At graduation the dean gave the group an honorary mention for an exemplary revision. Neri had thought mastery of a subject was the only way to earn such appreciation. Her contribution began with a specific point. The older wording was idiomatic, but the layout had hidden its meaning. The scholarship papers still went to the funding desk. The certificate went to a different office, and the new signs used the same terminology as the handbook.

四级汇总词汇 · 32中文译文

斜体字写出的入学要求

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一所学院为申请者办了入学说明会。内丽想拿到会计职业文凭和奖学金。院长在体育馆欢迎本科、研究生和博士项目的申请者。一位校友介绍了自己的创业经历。一位来自研究机构的学者谈了如何在数学上取得优异成绩，还有一位介绍了预科课程。内丽有夜校的结业证。听到老师提起研究生学位时，她放下了表格。一位招生顾问问，她觉得自己不符合哪项入学条件。

2内丽拿出招生手册。斜体印着的一行说，“研究生课程”必须进行分班面谈。下一段有一行普通字体，介绍的是职业课程的另一项要求。内丽误以为那段里的物主代词也指研究生课程。句子合乎语法，版面却掩盖了它们之间的联系。顾问请她带来成绩单，再说说她觉得每句话是什么意思。

3一位语言教师和内丽一起研究这几句。她做了简单标记，把每个名词写在指代它的代词上面。一个指示词指向研究生课程。下一行写的是另一个单数名词，复数代词则指学生们。一个副词改变了长陈述句的重点。改成一句简短的祈使句，指示就会清楚些。两人讨论了不定式在句中的作用，又挪了一个逗号。关键部分之间的关系标清楚后，内丽终于读懂了要求。

4问卷要求按字母顺序填写姓氏，还要写明申请的专业。内丽照抄了示例里的“经济学”，忘了在列表里找自己的会计专业。办公室实习生把表送给了另一位教授。这处错误很好改。顾问想知道，示例本身是否还有类似问题。他请一位认真的学生把纸上的示例和网页上的逐项对照。好几个示例用了首次申请的人可能不熟悉的词。

5他们又查了列出各类项目的一页。心理学学士和教育学副学士的学费不同。社会学博士项目可能提供研究资助。地理或新闻的入门课用的是另一个截止日期。内丽之前以为每个示例都适用于自己。对照表让她看清了真正相关的资格条件。一位动物学学生也来试用，看这张表是否适用于她。她还从中了解了入学后可以选择的专业方向。

6面谈时，一位研究人员问内丽有什么经验。她说起实习期间，一位做事认真的维修工教她核对付款和账单，她因此查出一笔重复收费。一位会计专家请她口头说明怎样修正。她的回答展现了分析能力，也比泛谈职业发展更切合问题。接着，他们谈到她是想专攻商务、跟创业者一起工作，还是继续读学术学位。

7修改后的手册先用一段话介绍每一种就读途径。一位社会学家检查示例是否默认每个申请者家境优越。学生报的记者则发现，奖学金截止日期放错了标题。院长请一位校董监督工作，也请两人合作。他们还删掉了一句原想带点反讽、读来却像在惊叹的话。学院在毕业典礼时把旧表格送进图书馆，留作案例。

8收到录取通知后，内丽也去试读新指示牌。一位口译员检查了其中一版，有编辑经验的学生检查了另一版。到毕业时，院长表扬了团队这次出色的修改。内丽以前以为，只有精通一门学科才能获得这样的认可。她的贡献起于一个具体的问题。旧写法符合语言习惯，只是版面让意思难以看清。奖学金材料仍交给资助窗口，证书交到另一个办公室，新的指示牌和手册用了同一套称呼。
